purpose: Govern external AI agents, MCP servers, provider skills and connected developer tools without allowing external live state or chat memory to replace SongChart repository authority.
precedence: PROJECT_AUTHORITY.md and current SongChart machine/domain contracts
current stage task contract and authored stage plan
live external resource state within the external system's declared authority scope
official provider documentation and installed provider skills

official_provider_integration_policy.rule: When a provider or platform becomes relevant to an active SongChart use case, evaluate its official MCP/agent integration before designing a custom MCP bridge.
evaluation_order: confirm the MCP/integration is officially owned or documented by the provider
compare it with already connected native tools, CLI, SDK and API access
prefer remote OAuth or provider-recommended authentication when it reduces secret handling
scope tools and permissions to the smallest useful read/development surface
record adoption, deferral or rejection in external-systems-registry.json
official_provider_integration_policy.adoption_threshold: Official availability alone is insufficient; adoption must reduce guessing, manual work or maintenance without creating duplicate authority or unnecessary runtime weight.

development.rule: Developer AI/MCP integrations may inspect and, when explicitly permitted, mutate development resources. Their installation must not create a production runtime dependency.

production.rule: Production mutations require the explicit release/operations workflow, least privilege and human-authorized intent. Development agents must not gain production mutation authority by being connected to an account.

product_ai.rule: Visitor-facing AI is a separate application capability. It must use governed SongChart read models/APIs, be retrieval-grounded and start read-only; development MCP connections are never exposed to visitors.

invariants: Git/GitHub plus repository contracts remain the source and delivery authority.
Laravel migrations remain the application schema-evolution authority.
Canonical music identity, reconciliation and provenance remain SongChart domain authorities.
External provider payloads, MCP responses and skills are evidence or product-specific operational state, not canonical schema authority.
MCP/agent credentials and provider secrets must never be committed to source or generated authority.
Live project IDs, branch IDs, account IDs, URLs and quotas are runtime facts unless a dedicated repository contract explicitly owns a stable identifier.
An MCP tool must not bypass the supported ./songchart lifecycle merely because a lower-level provider API is available.
No agent may silently fall back to a different development database, storage authority or environment after a configured external authority fails.
Generated repository authority is updated only through SongChart generation/reconciliation tooling.
Agent-local persistent memory is convenience state only and must yield to current repository and live-state evidence.

developer: edit the active synchronized development branch
operator: perform explicit development/staging infrastructure operations within declared provider scope
release: perform production mutations only through the release/operations workflow with explicit authorization

forbidden_shortcuts: direct production SQL as a replacement for Laravel migrations
direct canonical-data mutation from an external MCP without SongChart application/domain enforcement
committing generated provider credentials or connection strings
granting broad account mutation permissions only for convenience
installing optional AI routers/agents into production before a product or workflow requirement exists
installing both an official provider MCP and an overlapping custom/native bridge without documented unique responsibilities
